leads.name: Witte moerbei (White Mulberry) at the Van Abbemuseum
leads.reason: Register (LRMB nr 1690223, reason 'dendrologisch', age unknown) says monumental, but the Gemeente Eindhoven open-data 'bomen' dataset shows a Morus alba 1.4m from this point classed only 'Waardevol' (valuable), not 'Monumentaal', and planted 1970 (about 55 years old, not old by this project's bar). Sources conflict on both age and status; no visual or narrative evidence found that it is otherwise spectacular. Worth a second look if a photo or a stronger account turns up, but as it stands it does not clear the 'worth the walk' bar on its own.

leads.name: Papier moerbei (Paper Mulberry), Stadswandelpark
leads.reason: Only the LRMB register (nr 1690255, planted_band 1920-1930) places a tree here. The Gemeente Eindhoven open-data 'bomen' dataset has exactly one Papiermoerbei citywide, and it sits about 50m away near the Van Abbemuseum area (boomnummer 61975, planted 2002, 'Waardevol'), not at this coordinate, so it is not the same tree. A 60m radius search of the municipal dataset around this point found no paper mulberry at all (found instead a cluster of 1960-planted ginkgos, dawn redwoods and swamp cypresses, an arboretum-like planting near the Sterrenwacht). Two searches for independent confirmation (web search, municipal open data) came up empty. Second source not found; do not ship on the register alone.

leads.name: Spaanse eik (likely Northern Red Oak) near the Sterrenwacht, Stadswandelpark
leads.species: possibly Northern Red Oak (Quercus rubra); unconfirmed
leads.reason: Only the LRMB register (nr 1690256, planted_band 1930-1940, place given only as '* Nabij de Sterrenwacht, Stadspark, Eindhoven', visible='onbekend') places a tree here; the asterisk in the register's own place field suggests even the register is uncertain about the exact spot. No matching 'Spaanse eik' entry exists anywhere in the Gemeente Eindhoven open-data 'bomen' dataset citywide (checked by name, zero hits), and a 150m radius search around this coordinate found no Quercus rubra either, only a 1960s-era conifer/ginkgo planting. Web search found nothing specific. Second source not found and even the register's own location is marked uncertain; leave for a future pass with a site visit or better register scan.

leads.reason: The LRMB register lists several more entries at this same churchyard beyond nr 1694310 (already published as ein_008): nr 1680249 'Bruine beuk' explicitly carries n_trees=17, clearly a grove or hedge rather than one collectible point, and is blocked for that reason (see blocked list). Two more, nr 1695441 (bruine beuk, n_trees=2) and nr 1695440 (bruine beuk, n_trees not distinct), and nr 1680251 ('Slangenden', n_trees=2, an unclear register name, possibly corrupted text, standing in the former rectory's front garden) sit within roughly 150m of ein_008 and of each other. All are marked visitable=ja by the register but none has a recognition feature in the register data that would let a visitor tell it apart from ein_008 or from each other without standing there; publishing several near-identical copper beeches in one churchyard risks exactly the 'which trunk is worth the visit' problem this project tries to avoid (CLAUDE.md, the Nigatsu-do case). Left as a lead for a future pass with photos or a site visit that can describe what makes any one of them distinct.

leads.name: The Horse Chestnut of Prinsenhof
leads.age_estimate: roughly 120 years, from a registered planting date around 1910
verified_sources: Gemeente Eindhoven open data, dataset 'bomen', record near 51.435141,5.467914 (Dubbelbloemige paardenkastanje, Aesculus hippocastanum, plantjaar 1900)
leads.access: Free. Stands on the public street verge of Prinsenhof, a residential street in the Villapark conservation area (rijksbeschermd stadsgezicht).
leads.transport: Eindhoven Centraal station, about 20 minutes on foot; bus stops on Geldropseweg and Karel de Grotelaan are a few minutes' walk.
leads.story:
Eindhoven's monumental trees keep turning out to be Philips trees, and this one fits the pattern from an unusual angle: not a company gift but a plan. In 1907 the Villapark district went up as a garden suburb for Philips executives, laid out street by street with imported ornamental species, and the municipality's own tree management survey names this one specifically as a double-flowered cultivar of the ordinary horse chestnut, chosen on purpose rather than planted from whatever the nursery had spare that year.

The national monumental tree register and the city's separate street-tree inventory agree closely on where it stands and roughly when it went in, within a few years of 1900 either way. Two independently kept lists landing on the same tree and the same decade is rare enough here to be worth saying outright, since most entries in this project carry one source repeating what the other cannot check.

It stands on the street verge of Prinsenhof, in a district still recognisable as the plan that built it, protected now as a townscape rather than a nature reserve. The chestnut that gave Eindhoven its stadium tree and its avenue at the Wielewaal did not plant this one. Its own street did.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the doubled, fuller flower spikes in May, a cultivar the city's own tree survey names outright. It stands on the Prinsenhof verge opposite no. 5, in the Villapark district.

best_time.label: May, when its doubled flower spikes open fuller than an ordinary chestnut's

leads.removed_reason: Dead or felled per the register itself: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen nr 1690257 carries status 5, Dood/geveld (checked 2026-10-10 against the Bomenstichting ArcGIS layer). Inspector remark: "Omtrek respectievelijk 335 en 319 cm.  2020 Boom voor Prinsenhof 6, ten zuiden van beschreven exemplaar, in 2016 geveld vanwege scheefgroei en bloedziekte." Removed under the rule that a dead tree is never a collectible entry.

leads.name: The Southern Catalpa of Julianastraat
leads.age_estimate: roughly 120 years, from a registered planting date around 1910
leads.access: Free. Stands on the public street verge of Julianastraat in the Villapark conservation area.
leads.transport: Eindhoven Centraal station, about 20 minutes on foot; bus stops on Geldropseweg and Karel de Grotelaan are a few minutes' walk.
leads.story:
Only one source names this tree, and it is honest about not being sure of everything either. The national monumental tree register lists a Catalpa on Julianastraat, planted sometime in the 1900s, but gives no house number for it and marks its own visibility field unknown. The city's separate street-tree management inventory, which independently confirmed three of this cluster's other trees to within a few metres, has no Catalpa recorded anywhere near this point at all.

That gap does not mean the tree is wrong, only that it is unconfirmed a second way, which is the honest way to leave it rather than a reason to leave it out. A Catalpa bignonioides at roughly 120 years old would be a distinctive planting for this corner of the Villapark garden suburb, laid out from 1907 with deliberately varied ornamental species along its verges: broad heart-shaped leaves, white orchid-like flowers in early summer, and long thin seed pods that hang on through winter and give the tree its old nickname, the cigar tree.

If you know this tree or can measure it, tell us. A second source is the only thing standing between a flag and a confirmed entry.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the broad heart-shaped leaves and, in early summer, white orchid-like flowers; the long thin pods that follow give it the old name cigar tree. It stands on Julianastraat, Villapark.

best_time.label: July, when the white orchid-like flowers open across the crown

leads.removed_reason: Dead or felled per the register itself: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen nr 1680793 carries status 5, Dood/geveld (checked 2026-10-10 against the Bomenstichting ArcGIS layer). Inspector remark: "Gerooid ten behoeve van woningbouw in 1992!" Removed under the rule that a dead tree is never a collectible entry.

leads.name: The Horse Chestnut of Palingstraat
leads.age_estimate: roughly 120 years, from a registered planting date around 1910

location.address: Palingstraat / Karel de Grotelaan, Villapark, Eindhoven

leads.access: Free. Stands on the public road verge at the Palingstraat/Karel de Grotelaan junction, owner category 'gemeente' (municipality) in the register.
leads.transport: Eindhoven Centraal station, about 20 minutes on foot; bus stops on Geldropseweg and Karel de Grotelaan are a few minutes' walk.
leads.story:
This chestnut and the double-flowered one on Prinsenhof, about 250 metres away, are two different trees carrying the same common name and the same rough age, which is worth saying plainly so nobody mistakes one for the other. Only the national monumental tree register names this one: a white horse chestnut on the public road verge at the junction of Palingstraat and Karel de Grotelaan, planted somewhere in the 1900s, owned and maintained by the municipality.

The city's own separate street-tree survey, checked within 25 metres of this spot, records no horse chestnut here at all, only a silver lime from 1920 and a black lime from 1985 a short distance off. That is not evidence the register is wrong, registers and management inventories are compiled differently and do not always list the same trees, but it means this one stands on one source rather than two, and the entry says so honestly.

It grows in the Villapark district, the Philips-era garden suburb planted from 1907, on a street corner rather than in a garden, open to anyone walking past.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by standing at the Palingstraat/Karel de Grotelaan corner rather than on Prinsenhof, about 250 metres from the district's other monumental horse chestnut.
leads.removed_reason: Dead or felled per the register itself: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen nr 1680794 carries status 5, Dood/geveld (checked 2026-10-10 against the Bomenstichting ArcGIS layer). Inspector remark: "Na veel inspanning van de buurtbewoners gespaard tijdens wegrenovatie en nieuwbouw (3 juni 1998. Boom is in oktober 2006 gekapt. Boom leverde gevaar op i.v.m. aantasting tonderzwam." Removed under the rule that a dead tree is never a collectible entry.
